word:greek-nt:G0002.explanation: Aaron is a personal name for Moses’ brother.

word:greek-nt:G0118.explanation: This word means “to compete” or “to compete in a contest.” It describes active participation in a contest, emphasizing the effort of striving against others according to the contest’s requirements. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both instances appearing in 2 Timothy 2:5. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage, but the central idea remains competing in an organized contest rather than merely making an attempt or expressing a desire.

word:greek-nt:G0147.explanation: Aischrokerdōs means greedily, with an eagerness for dishonest gain.

word:greek-nt:G0235.explanation: Alla means but, and it connects contrasting statements.

word:greek-nt:G0288.explanation: Ampelos means a vine or grapevine.

word:greek-nt:G0396.explanation: Anatrepō means to overturn, overthrow, or subvert.

word:greek-nt:G0406.explanation: Andreas is the personal name Andrew. Andrew was Simon Peter’s brother and one of the apostles.

word:greek-nt:G0473.explanation: Anti means instead of. It can also mark an exchange, where one thing is given in return for another.

word:greek-nt:G0499.explanation: Antitypos means a representation that corresponds to a pattern.

word:greek-nt:G0648.explanation: This Greek New Testament verb means “to make an opening in a roof” or “to unroof.” It describes the action of removing or opening part of a roof, functioning as an action word rather than naming the roof itself. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at Mark 2:4. Its precise force in that verse is understood from the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is the act of opening or uncovering a roof.

word:greek-nt:G0815.explanation: The word means “childless”: having no children. It describes a person who has no child. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both in Luke 20:28–29, and is rendered “childless” each time. The word therefore names the condition of having no children. Its precise role in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning remains clear.

word:greek-nt:G0961.explanation: Beroiaios means belonging to Berea, or Berean.

word:greek-nt:G1092.explanation: Geōrgos means a farmer or husbandman.

word:greek-nt:G1126.explanation: This word refers to an “old wives’ tale”—a traditional story or saying treated as unreliable or unworthy of serious attention. It appears once in the Greek New Testament, at 1 Timothy 4:7. The word itself describes the kind of tale being dismissed, rather than naming a person or presenting a teaching to believe. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central meaning is clear: a fanciful or foolish traditional story.

word:greek-nt:G1153.explanation: This word refers to a person from Damascus, identifying someone by connection with that city. It can be understood as “Damascene” or “from Damascus.” In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 2 Corinthians 11:32, and its meaning is geographical rather than a description of a person’s character or beliefs. The word therefore identifies a Damascene—someone associated with Damascus—without, by itself, explaining anything more about that person.

word:greek-nt:G1229.explanation: Diangellō means to announce or proclaim news.

word:greek-nt:G1324.explanation: Didymos means “the Twin” and is the Greek name used for Thomas.

word:greek-nt:G1391.explanation: Doxa means glory. It can describe the honor or renown associated with kingdoms. It can also refer to divine splendor and to glory given to God.

word:greek-nt:G1445.explanation: Hebraios means a Hebrew or refers to Hebrews.

word:greek-nt:G1522.explanation: Eisakouō means to hear. It can also mean to listen to or heed.

word:greek-nt:G1580.explanation: Ekkomizō means to carry out, as when a dead person is carried out for burial.

word:greek-nt:G1603.explanation: Ekplēroō means to fill completely or fulfill in every particular.

word:greek-nt:G1676.explanation: Hellenisti means in the Greek language—in Greek.

word:greek-nt:G1751.explanation: Eneimi means to be in or within.

word:greek-nt:G1849.explanation: Exousia means authority or power. It can describe authority to heal.

word:greek-nt:G1904.explanation: Eperchomai means to come to or arrive, and it can also mean to come upon something. It can describe an attack, as when a stronger person attacks someone.

word:greek-nt:G2008.explanation: Epitimao means to rebuke or admonish. It can also mean to warn.

word:greek-nt:G2057.explanation: Hermas is the name of a Roman Christian mentioned among a group of brothers.

word:greek-nt:G2101.explanation: Euarestos means acceptable or well-pleasing, especially to God. It can describe service acceptable to God and a sacrifice well-pleasing to God.

word:greek-nt:G2233.explanation: Hēgeomai means to lead or govern, and it can also mean to think, suppose, or consider. The leadership sense describes a governor ruling over people, while the thinking sense can describe considering gains to be a loss.

word:greek-nt:G2310.explanation: Themelios means a foundation stone or foundation, the base laid beneath a building. A house founded on rock remains firm, while a house without a foundation falls.

word:greek-nt:G2440.explanation: Himation means a long, flowing outer garment or item of clothing.

word:greek-nt:G2505.explanation: Katha means “just as” or “as,” linking an action with what was commanded.

word:greek-nt:G2619.explanation: The word means “to cover”: to place something over another thing so it is covered. It describes the action of covering rather than the object used for covering. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs three times, all within two verses in 1 Corinthians 11. Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding wording, but its central meaning remains the act of covering. The word should therefore be understood according to this basic action, without adding a broader meaning not present in the context.

word:greek-nt:G2686.explanation: Katasophizomai means to deal craftily with or outwit.

word:greek-nt:G2772.explanation: Kerma means a small coin or small change.

word:greek-nt:G2866.explanation: Kompsoteron means in better health, or getting better.

word:greek-nt:G3025.explanation: Lēnos means a winepress. It can also refer to a trough.

word:greek-nt:G3098.explanation: Magog is a name used for a people. It can also name a country.

word:greek-nt:G3120.explanation: Malakos means soft. When used of persons, it can describe someone as effeminate.

word:greek-nt:G3182.explanation: Methyskō means to become drunk. It can also mean to make people drunk, as people are made drunk with wine.

word:greek-nt:G3344.explanation: Μεταστραφήσεται means to be turned or changed.

word:greek-nt:G3407.explanation: Misthios means a paid worker or hired servant.

word:greek-nt:G3458.explanation: Mylos means a millstone. It can also refer to a mill used for grinding.

word:greek-nt:G3641.explanation: Oligon means few when referring to a small number. It can also mean little, describing a small distance.

word:greek-nt:G3775.explanation: Ous means the ear and can also refer to the faculty of perception.

word:greek-nt:G3832.explanation: Panoikei means with one's whole household or family.

word:greek-nt:G3959.explanation: The word refers to “Patara,” a proper name in the Greek New Testament. It does not describe an action, quality, or person; it identifies a named place. This word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Acts 21:1. Its basic meaning is simply the place-name Patara, while the word’s particular significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and context.

word:greek-nt:G4042.explanation: Perioche means a section or passage of Scripture.

word:greek-nt:G4107.explanation: This word describes a “wanderer” or something “wandering”—moving without a settled course or destination. It can identify a person who roams or describe movement that lacks direction. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Jude 1:13, so its broader use must be understood from this basic sense rather than from several biblical examples. The word emphasizes unsettled movement and the absence of a fixed path.

word:greek-nt:G4158.explanation: Podērēs means reaching to the feet, describing a floor-length garment.

word:greek-nt:G4341.explanation: Proskaleō means to call someone to oneself or summon them.

word:greek-nt:G4420.explanation: Pteryx means a wing or pinion.

word:greek-nt:G4482.explanation: This word means “to flow” or “to overflow,” describing something moving onward like a stream or water pouring out. It expresses continuous movement rather than a fixed condition. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in John 7:38, so its precise force there depends on the surrounding verse and passage. The basic idea remains movement that proceeds outward, with “overflow” highlighting abundance or fullness when the context calls for it.

word:greek-nt:G4525.explanation: This word means “to be unsettled” or “to shake.” It describes being disturbed, agitated, or moved from steadiness rather than remaining calm and secure. The word appears once in the Greek New Testament, in 1 Thessalonians 3:3. Its basic sense concerns a person being shaken or unsettled, while the surrounding verse determines the particular nature of that disturbance. The meaning is therefore broader than physical movement alone and can describe inward instability or distress.

word:greek-nt:G4763.explanation: Strēniaō means to live luxuriously. It can also describe reveling or riotous living.

word:greek-nt:G4789.explanation: Synklēronomos means a joint heir—one who inherits together with others.

word:greek-nt:G4811.explanation: Sykophanteō means to accuse falsely or defraud. It can also mean to extort.

word:greek-nt:G4936.explanation: Syntrecho means to run together or run with.

word:greek-nt:G4943.explanation: This word means “to join in helping” or “to join to help.” It describes actively cooperating with others so that assistance is shared rather than given alone. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in 2 Corinthians 1:11, and functions as an expression of participating in help. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but the central idea is united assistance: people joining together in support of a need or work.

word:greek-nt:G5179.explanation: Typos means a figure or pattern. It can also mean an example to follow.

word:greek-nt:G5193.explanation: Hyalinos means glassy or made of glass.

word:greek-nt:G5261.explanation: Hypogrammos means an example or pattern.

word:greek-nt:G5315.explanation: φαγεῖν means to eat or partake of food.

word:greek-nt:G5423.explanation: This word means “deceiver”—someone who misleads others rather than dealing with them truthfully. It identifies a person by the harmful effect of his words or influence: he leads people away from what is true. In the Greek New Testament, this word occurs once, in Titus 1:10. The reference identifies where the word appears, but its precise force in that verse is understood from the surrounding passage and verse text.

word:greek-nt:G5456.explanation: Phōnē means a sound or voice. It can describe a voice recognized by those who hear it or voices raised in urgent appeal.

word:greek-nt:G5584.explanation: Pselaphao means to touch, feel, or handle. It can also mean to feel or grope for what one is seeking.

word:greek-nt:G5614.explanation: Hosanna is a cry for help or a cry of happiness.
